mappings.note: Range of vision of a NORMAL eye (25 cm to infinity) - the span over which accommodation works, LO-4, not a defect.
Naming the common defects of vision is the recall half of LO-5; LO-4 never mentions defects.
Definition of hypermetropia - LO-5 names this defect explicitly.
Convex lens for hypermetropia - LO-5's 'selects the type of lens that corrects each'. Stored concept tag 'Human Eye Structure' points at LO-4 and is wrong.
Definition of myopia - LO-5.
Concave lens for myopia - LO-5's lens-selection clause. Stored concept tag 'Human Eye Structure' is wrong.
A defect that spoils BOTH near and far vision is presbyopia, the third defect named in LO-5. Stored concept tag 'Near and Far Points' would point at LO-4, but a defect is present here.
Bifocal lens for the same presbyopic case - the lens-selection clause of LO-5.
Image formation by a MYOPIC eye plus the remedy; a defect diagram, LO-5. Stored concept tag 'Rainbow Formation' is wrong.
Causes of myopia (elongated eyeball, over-curved lens) - explaining the defect, LO-5.
Far point at 2 m gives -0.5 D; naming and correcting the defect is LO-5. Stem is OCR-damaged ('d short sighted', 'power of less required').
Infers the defect from a concave prescription - LO-5's lens-defect pairing, run backwards.
Infers hypermetropia from a convex prescription - the same LO-5 pairing as the previous item, opposite sign.
Angle of deviation marked on a prism ray diagram - the prism ray-diagram apparatus of C 8.1-LO-3.
Reproducing the colours on the screen after a prism is the dispersion spectrum, C 8.1-LO-3. DEFECT: the stem refers to a diagram that is not in the text, so the item is not answerable as stored.
Definition of dispersion - the head clause of C 8.1-LO-3.
Cause of dispersion (different refractive index, hence different deviation, per colour) - the mechanism inside LO-3, not scattering. Stem OCR: 'came' for 'cause'.
Ordering VIBGYOR by wavelength is what fixes the order of the dispersed spectrum, so LO-3 rather than the scattering outcome LO-4.
Red has the greatest wavelength and is least deviated - a spectrum-order fact belonging to dispersion, LO-3.
Violet has the least wavelength and is most deviated - the other end of the same LO-3 spectrum-order fact.
Least and most deviated colours through a prism - deviation is the prism behaviour described by LO-3. Stem OCR: 'glass 4 prism'.
The natural phenomenon caused by dispersion is the rainbow - both halves of C 8.1-LO-3 in one item.
Refraction, dispersion and internal reflection in a raindrop - the rainbow clause of LO-3. Scattering is not one of the three, so LO-4 is false.
Maximum and minimum deviation colours in a prism - LO-3.
More deviation means larger refractive index and lower speed in the glass - the physical cause of dispersion, LO-3.
Definition of scattering - the head clause of C 8.1-LO-4, distinct from dispersion in LO-3.

Slow adjustment on entering a dim room is the iris opening the pupil - a structure-and-function question about the eye, LO-4. Stored concept tag 'Scattering of Light' is wrong; no scattering is involved.
Relaxed ciliary muscles give the longer focal length - the accommodation mechanism in LO-4, asked about a normal eye.

Binocular vision - wider field and depth perception - is not the structure/accommodation of LO-4 nor a defect in LO-5, so it honestly reaches only the competency C 2.3. Cited at competency level deliberately rather than forced onto LO-4.
Contrasts a fixed glass lens with the eye lens that refocuses for every object distance - precisely LO-4's 'explains how the lens accommodates to focus at different distances'.
Accommodation plus the least distance of distinct vision, both properties of the normal eye - LO-4.
Short-sightedness defined and corrected - myopia and its concave lens, LO-5.
Long-sightedness defined and corrected - hypermetropia and its convex lens, LO-5.
Presbyopia, its cause and its correction - the third defect named in LO-5.
An old person failing at both ends is presbyopia needing bifocals; LO-5 covers naming it and choosing the lens.
A -1 D prescription means a concave lens and myopia - LO-5's lens-defect pairing. Stored concept tag 'Power of Accommodation' is wrong; no accommodation is asked.
A positive (convex) prescription means hypermetropia - same LO-5 pairing. Stem OCR-damaged: '+ IS D' for '+1.5 D'.
Image distance is fixed by the retina while the lens changes focal length - the accommodation clause of LO-4.
Weakened ciliary muscles and a stiff lens name presbyopia, and the item asks for the bifocal lens and its structure - LO-5, even though the mechanism described is accommodation failing.
Dispersion defined, its cause, and the prism ray diagram - all three clauses of C 8.1-LO-3.
Why each colour has its own angle of deviation - the mechanism of dispersion through a prism, LO-3.
Separation and recombination of the spectrum with a second prism - dispersion, LO-3.
Two identical prisms recombining white light; a prism-dispersion demonstration, LO-3.
Newton's two-prism experiment showing white light is composite - the classic dispersion proof, LO-3.
Seven colours through a prism plus which deviates least - dispersion and deviation order, LO-3.
Rainbow ray diagram and the conditions for seeing one - the rainbow clause of C 8.1-LO-3.
Spray from a fountain with the sun behind you produces a rainbow - the rainbow clause of LO-3 applied to a non-rain source of drops.
Rainbow requires suspended droplets - LO-3's rainbow clause. DEFECT: exact duplicate of qid:86819 in this same chapter.
Atmospheric refraction described and used for the advanced sunrise and delayed sunset - both clauses of C 5.3-LO-2.
Sun visible after it has actually set - the advanced-sunrise/delayed-sunset application in C 5.3-LO-2. DEFECT: near-duplicate of qid:86881.
The oval sun near the horizon comes from unequal refraction of the upper and lower limbs - atmospheric refraction, LO-2 of C 5.3, not the colour change that scattering explains.
Blue sky by scattering - C 8.1-LO-4. DEFECT: duplicate of qid:86820.
Red for stop signals because red scatters least - a scattering application, LO-4.
No atmosphere means no scattering and a black sky - the blue-sky mechanism of LO-4 argued by removing it.
Sun's colour at sunrise/sunset versus noon is set by path length and hence scattering, LO-4, not by the refraction that shifts its apparent time. DEFECT: duplicate of qid:86821.
Parts of the eye, their functions and image formation on the retina - the structure clause of LO-4 in full.
Myopia defined, two causes, and the correction ray diagram - LO-5 across all three parts.
Hypermetropia defined, two causes, correction diagram - the hypermetropia half of LO-5.
Correction of myopia by a concave lens, with diagram - LO-5's lens-selection clause.
Refraction through a prism and the definition of the angle of deviation - the prism ray diagram that underpins C 8.1-LO-3's dispersion account.
